**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Affected part: stems (multiple soybean stems)
- Key features: reddish-brown to tan discoloration running along the lower stem cortex/epidermis, longitudinal browning pattern, hairy soybean stems with significant external tissue browning near/above soil line

**Comparison with Rhizoctonia reference:**
The reference shows reddish-brown lesions on lower stems/hypocotyls — the bottom-left panel especially shows a close-up of reddish-brown stem canker that closely matches the test image's external stem discoloration pattern. The test image's multiple stems with reddish-brown cortex browning near the soil line aligns well with Rhizoctonia root rot/stem canker symptoms.

This matches Rhizoctonia better than Phytophthora (which tends to be darker chocolate-brown, water-soaked, progressing from soil line) or Brown Stem Rot (which is primarily internal pith browning requiring a cross-section to see).
